summary: Primary-source verify each remaining audit finding per host (read-only); classify real / non-gap / unverifiable + exact fix spec

real.verdict: REAL GAP: Amazon Q Developer CLI documentation clearly shows that **agents** (user-authored, agent-format.md) are a primary feature stored in per-agent JSON files, and the prompt library feature (contexts) exists at ~/.aws/amazonq/prompts/. The adapter states 'no documented user-authored commands/skills/subagents directory verified for Amazon Q' but agents ARE documented and user-authored. Whether mapped to capabilities.supportsSkills or a new supportsAgents flag, the adapter should expose that Amazon Q supports custom agent definitions. Agents contain name, description, custom prompt, tool allowlists, hooks, and resources — analogous to 'skills' in the agent-connector abstraction.
real.evidence: From agent-format.md: 'The agent configuration file for each agent is a JSON file. The filename (without the .json extension) becomes the agent's name.' Agents support: name, description, prompt (inline or file://), mcpServers, tools, toolAliases, allowedTools, toolsSettings, resources, hooks, useLegacyMcpJson, model. From prompts doc: 'Prompts are saved in the ~/.aws/amazonq/prompts folder.' This is a documented, public surface.
real.fixSpec: Update amazon-q adapter capabilities: either (a) set supportsSkills: true and wire supportsAgents: true as a new custom capability alongside it, documenting that Amazon Q agents map to skill-like constructs; OR (b) add supportsAgents: true as a dedicated capability. The adapter should declare memoryTargets() for agents if memory is to be injected into agent definitions. However, the minimal fix to address the audit claim is: set capabilities.supportsSkills = true (or add supportsAgents flag and set it true) with a comment that Amazon Q agents are stored per-user/per-project and are user-authored agent definitions (not installed by AC, but AC could support injecting memory or context into them in a future phase). Update the comment on line 131 to acknowledge: 'Amazon Q supports agents (stored in ~/.aws/amazonq/cli-agents/*.json or .amazonq/cli-agents/*.json per-project) and prompts (~/aws/amazonq/prompts/). Agent wiring not yet implemented (future work).'

The comment is factually wrong, though the deferred implementation status (supportsSubagents=false) is intentional pending SDK-schema-coupled rendering.
real.evidence: Codebuff docs state: 'Create a new TypeScript file in .agents/ directory... .agents/my-custom-agent.ts' (www.codebuff.com/docs/agents/creating-new-agents). platform-data.ts line 196-198: 'codebuff: subagents=true [high] — user-defined TypeScript agents in .agents/'. landing-page-gap-backlog.md line 51-52 (DEFERRED section): 'codebuff subagents — confirmed real, but an executable .agents/*.ts AgentDefinition module (SDK-schema-coupled)'.
real.fixSpec: Update the misleading comment at src/adapters/codebuff/index.ts:124 from 'Commands / subagents have no native Codebuff surface' to 'Commands have no native Codebuff surface. Subagents are natively supported as executable .agents/*.ts AgentDefinition modules (SDK-schema-coupled render deferred)'. No code change needed—this is a documentation-only fix. The supportsSubagents=false capability flag is intentionally correct (subagents are deferred, not unsupported).

real.verdict: CONFIRMED: Three hook events (SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, Stop) are supported by Goose's Open Plugins runtime per official docs, but the adapter marks these capabilities as FALSE, causing them to be warn-skipped during installation instead of written to hooks.json. The parseEvent() method has full implementations for all three, confirming the adapter is capable at runtime but gated by incorrect capability flags.
real.evidence: Goose documentation (https://goose-docs.ai/blog/2026/05/14/goose-hooks/) explicitly lists supported events: 'SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure'. However, adapter capabilities (src/adapters/goose/index.ts lines 170-201) declares: sessionEnd: false (line 179), userPromptSubmit: false (line 180), stop: false (line 181). Despite these false flags, parseEvent() (lines 735-765) contains complete case implementations for all three events, and the wire protocol interface (GooseWireInput, lines 140-163) includes all required fields (reason, prompt, stop_hook_active).
real.fixSpec:
In src/adapters/goose/index.ts, update the readonly capabilities object (lines 170-201) to mark three events as supported:
- Line 179: change `sessionEnd: false,` to `sessionEnd: true,`
- Line 180: change `userPromptSubmit: false,` to `userPromptSubmit: true,`
- Line 181: change `stop: false,` to `stop: true,`

No changes required to EVENT_CAPABILITY map, parseEvent(), or wire protocol handling — all are already correct and complete. This fix removes the gating that prevents installHooks() from writing these three events to hooks.json. The existing test at tests/adapters/wave3.test.ts line 348 (which expects UserPromptSubmit to be skipped) must be updated to expect installation success instead of warn.

real.verdict: Confirmed genuine gap: Kimi has a documented plugin system that agent-connector does not currently install or manage.
real.evidence: Official Kimi Code CLI documentation (https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code-cli/customization/plugins.html) states: 'A plugin is a directory or zip file containing a manifest. The manifest can be placed at either of the following locations: <plugin_root>/kimi.plugin.json or <plugin_root>/plugin.json'. Supported fields include: skills, sessionStart.skill, mcpServers, skillInstructions. Kimi adapter code explicitly acknowledges this gap at lines 54-55: 'Kimi also has a PLUGIN system (`<base>/plugins/<name>/kimi.plugin.json`), not yet surfaced.'
real.fixSpec: Add plugin support to KimiAdapter by: (1) add capability flag 'supportsPlugins: true' to the capabilities object (line 210-250); (2) implement installPlugins(ctx: InstallContext): ChangeRecord[] method to write plugin manifest entries to $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/<id>/kimi.plugin.json with name, version, skills (relative paths), sessionStart.skill, mcpServers (from connector.server), and skillInstructions (from connector.instructions if available); (3) implement uninstallPlugins(ctx: InstallContext): ChangeRecord[] to remove the managed plugin directory; (4) add plugin diagnostic health checks (detectInstalled should also look for plugins/ dir; getHealthChecks should verify plugin manifest presence if plugins are declared); (5) coordinate with skill installation — plugins can bundle skills, so installSkills should validate no path conflicts between <skillDir> and plugin skill paths.

real.verdict: The finding is PARTIALLY REAL. OpenCode (which MiMoCode forks 1:1) does expose additional lifecycle hooks beyond the 3 wired. The adapter correctly wires only PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SessionStart but leaves userPromptSubmit, stop, and notification all false. The OpenCode plugin docs (platform-research.json lines 651-681) confirm chat.message, session.idle, and session.error are real, documented, native events. However, the permission.ask sub-claim is REFUTED by the existing audit (line 237-239), which notes OpenCode issues #7006 and #19927 show permission.ask is defined in SDK types but never reliably triggered.
real.sourceVerified: https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ (verified via platform-research.json lines 651-681: hook_types array lists chat.message [654], chat.params [655], session.idle [659], session.error [663], and permission.ask [656])
real.evidence: Platform-research.json lines 654-663 enumerate OpenCode's native hooks: 'chat.message', 'chat.params', 'session.idle', 'session.error'. Line 657 also lists 'event (generic dispatcher; switch on event.type)'. The adapter's EVENT_TO_MIMOCODE (mimo-code/index.ts lines 110-116) wires only 3 events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart) and capabilities (lines 150-155) set userPromptSubmit:false, stop:false, notification:false, despite session.idle and chat.message being confirmed real.
real.fixSpec: For userPromptSubmit: (1) add EVENT_TO_MIMOCODE['UserPromptSubmit'] = 'chat.message'; (2) set capabilities.userPromptSubmit = true; (3) add a handler in buildPluginSource for 'chat.message': async (input, output) => { payload = {sessionId, projectDir}; res = bridge('UserPromptSubmit', payload); if (res.updatedPrompt && output) output.prompt = res.updatedPrompt; }. For stop: (1) add EVENT_TO_MIMOCODE['Stop'] = 'session.idle'; (2) set capabilities.stop = true; (3) add a handler for 'session.idle': async (input, output) => { payload = {sessionId, projectDir}; res = bridge('Stop', payload); if (res.decision === 'block') throw new Error(res.reason || 'Stopped'); }. Note: MiMoCode's native plugin shape mirrors OpenCode's exactly (chat.message async (input, output) signature, session.idle event handler), so no bridge payload shape changes needed. Skip permission.ask entirely per upstream reliability issues.

real.verdict: UserPromptSubmit is unmapped but could be supported via before_prompt_build, which fires at every prompt assembly per user turn. The adapter currently marks userPromptSubmit:false and does not add UserPromptSubmit to EVENT_TO_OPENCLAW, causing any declared UserPromptSubmit hook to be reported as 'unsupported here'.
real.evidence: OpenClaw docs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/docs/plugins/hooks.md) confirm: before_prompt_build 'receives the current prompt and session messages' and can return 'prependContext, appendContext, systemPrompt, prependSystemContext, or appendSystemContext' — the standard context-injection contract. It fires 'before the model call' on every agent turn. The adapter already uses before_prompt_build for SessionStart context injection (lines 1266-1270 in index.ts).
real.fixSpec: 1. Add UserPromptSubmit: 'before_prompt_build' to EVENT_TO_OPENCLAW map (line 160-172). 2. Set userPromptSubmit: true in capabilities (line 245). 3. In buildPluginSource (starting line 1061), add a handler that: (a) receives the UserPromptSubmit event with prompt field, (b) bridges it via bridge('UserPromptSubmit', {prompt, sessionId, projectDir}), (c) returns additionalContext from the response as appendSystemContext. The handler should coexist with the SessionStart-injected context (use a separate pendingPromptContext variable so both can be injected into before_prompt_build without double-injection). Test: declare UserPromptSubmit, verify hookDetail() reports 'UserPromptSubmit' mapped, verify generated plugin registers a before_prompt_build handler that checks for pendingPromptContext from UserPromptSubmit and injects it alongside SessionStart context.

real.verdict: OpenCode HAS a native decision-capable `permission.ask` hook (confirmed in /dev/packages/plugin/src/index.ts line 262: "permission.ask"?: (input: Permission, output: { status: "ask" | "deny" | "allow" }) => Promise<void>). The adapter deliberately leaves it unwired with the adapter comment explaining 'E1 keeps this adapter degrade-only' (lines 157-164). The capability flag permissionRequest is unset (defaults to false), and the generated plugin never references permission.ask. This is a real gap: if a connector declares PermissionRequest hook events, the adapter silently skips them without warning.

The bridge handler should mutate output.status field per the OpenCode signature.

real.verdict: SessionStart is mapped only via the experimental.chat.system.transform surrogate hook (line 112 comment confirms '#14808 / #5409' as the source of truth). OpenCode lacks a true SessionStart hook. The surrogate injects additionalContext into the system prompt array (output.system.splice(1, 0, ...)) but does not receive full session lifecycle signals (session ID at creation time, session metadata, etc.). If OpenCode adds a native session-start hook in the future, the surrogate (which is tied to the system-prompt transformation point in the chat flow) is weaker than a proper lifecycle hook because it only injects prompt-level context, not session-level control.
real.evidence: Adapter line 46-48: 'SessionStart → "experimental.chat.system.transform" (no real SessionStart hook upstream — #14808/#5409; this is the verified surrogate context-mode uses; we inject additionalContext into output.system).' GitHub issue title confirmed: 'Plugin event listener for "session.created" not firing · Issue #14808 · anomalyco/opencode'. OpenCode Hooks interface shows no 'session.start' or 'SessionStart' field; experimental.chat.system.transform exists at line 313-317 of index.ts.
real.sourceVerified: GitHub https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14808 (confirmed session.created event not firing) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/packages/plugin/src/index.ts (shows experimental.chat.system.transform at lines 313-317 with no true SessionStart hook) and /home/ubuntu/workspace/github/agent-connector/src/adapters/opencode/index.ts (lines 46-48, 112, 815-831)
real.fixSpec: This is a host limitation, not an adapter gap. The adapter correctly uses the only available injection point. The fix is at the OpenCode platform level: implement a true 'session.start' or 'session.created' hook in the Hooks interface (anomalyco/opencode repository). Until then, the adapter must continue using experimental.chat.system.transform. For forward compatibility: add a comment in EVENT_TO_OPENCODE stating 'TODO: migrate to true session.start hook when OpenCode issue #14808/#5409 is resolved' so future maintainers know to switch the mapping when OpenCode adds native support. No adapter code change is needed at this time; this is a documented host limitation.

nonGap.verdict: The adapter correctly marks stop capability as false. While Gemini's AfterAgent hook carries a stop_hook_active field and can set continue:false to halt a session, this is semantically distinct from a Stop event hook. AfterAgent fires after model response generation for validation/retry logic, whereas Stop should fire when a user requests interruption. The stop_hook_active field is a state indicator (whether already retrying) rather than a functional Stop equivalent. The adapter author explicitly documented this decision in comments (line 23: 'Stop has no Gemini equivalent'). Using AfterAgent to implement Stop would misuse a post-response hook for pre-interruption semantics.
nonGap.evidence: Gemini CLI docs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/main/docs/hooks/reference.md): AfterAgent fires 'once per turn after the model generates its final response' with input fields including 'stop_hook_active (boolean)' to indicate 'if this hook is already running as part of a retry sequence' and output field 'continue: Set to false to stop the session'. agent-connector platform-research.json (line 1044): confirms AfterAgent carries 'stop_hook_active' in payload. agent-connector adapter (line 23): explicitly states 'Stop has no Gemini equivalent and is reported as a warn/skip at install'. core/types.ts: StopEvent has field 'stopHookActive?: boolean' — a state indicator, not a control mechanism.

nonGap.verdict: The adapter is correct. Pi does have a lifecycle event system, but NOT in the 'json-stdio or ts-plugin sense' that the adapter references.
